narration.text: [energetic] You just got the easiest night job in town: watching an empty laundromat for double pay. [suspicious] But the owner writes you three rules on a dryer sheet, and his hand won't stop shaking.
[serious] Rule one: lock the front door at midnight. Don't open it for anyone, [amused] even a sweet old lady knocking politely with a basket of dripping wet laundry.
[dramatic] Rule two: at two o'clock, washer number nine starts spinning all by itself. [serious] Never open its door, no matter what you hear knocking from inside the drum.
[knowing] Rule three: if a customer asks your name, give a fake one. [serious] Never say your real name out loud, and never let anyone read your name badge.

[upbeat] Last winter, a sleepy student named Mia worked the late shift. At eleven, a sweet old lady folding towels asked her name, and Mia just told her. [dramatic] The lady smiled and tied a little tag to washer nine.
[serious] At two o'clock, it started spinning.
[dramatic] In the morning, the owner found Mia's uniform tumbling inside the drum. [ironic] Behind the counter, the old lady wore her name badge and waved. "Hi, I'm Mia!"
